items.title: SQLite foreign_keys pragma never enabled — declared cascade FKs not actually enforced
items.notes: Found 2026-07-20 by the BUG-33 schema brief. Original claim: src/backend/db/index.ts has no `PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON` anywhere, and plain SQLite disables FK enforcement by default per-connection — concluded that declared cascades were decorative only. CORRECTED 2026-07-20, same session: the BUG-32 backend brief independently hit this exact question (a real production 500 on deleting a place with items still referencing it — only possible if the FK constraint IS being enforced) and empirically verified via an isolated @libsql/client script that FK enforcement is ON by default with this driver, no explicit pragma needed. COO independently reproduced the same test directly (DELETE against a referenced parent row failed with SQLITE_CONSTRAINT_FOREIGNKEY) and confirms this. The original claim was a correct fact about the plain SQLite C library that doesn't hold for @libsql/client specifically — this codebase's actual driver. No orphaned-row risk exists; closing as not-a-bug. The real bug this surfaced (items.trip_place_id has no onDelete behavior specified, so deleting a place with items throws a 500 instead of cascading or reassigning) was fixed independently in PR #166 (BUG-32) via reassign-to-null rather than cascade-delete, to preserve logged items.

items.title: items.carriedFromItemId has no onDelete FK behavior — trip deletion 500s if a carried-forward item still references it
items.notes: Found 2026-07-21 by the WP-03/WP-04 Frontend brief (PR #208) while writing E2E coverage for the carried-forward tag — pre-existing defect, not introduced by that PR. Symptom: DELETE /api/trips/:id 500s if any of the trip's items was ever used as a carry-forward source (items.carried_from_item_id) for an item in ANY other trip, including trips since modified/locked/unlocked (the reference persists independent of trip status). Root cause: carriedFromItemId is a self-referencing FK (.references(() => items.id)) with no .onDelete(...) clause — SQLite/@libsql FK enforcement (confirmed ON by default, see BUG-38) defaults to RESTRICT. Proposed fix (Frontend's suggestion, needs Architect/Database sign-off): add { onDelete: 'set null' } — semantically correct, clears provenance without cascading the delete — requires a migration (db:generate + db:migrate) per the schema-change rule. Also check whether deleting an individual source item directly (not just whole-trip deletion) hits the same constraint, if that's ever exposed as its own operation. User impact: deleting a trip after one of its items was carried forward elsewhere produces an unrecoverable 500 today. Not blocking WP-03/WP-04 (the new E2E test cleans up in the correct order to avoid destabilizing the suite). GitHub issue #209. Full discovery write-up: jobs/frontend/park-docs/20260721-FRONTEND-wp03wp04-park.txt.

IMPLEMENTED (PR #181, merged): Turso + Railway hosts added to init-firewall.sh; .env.agent-diagnostics (gitignored) with both Turso tokens (verified via JWT claim inspection — distinct per-database `rid`, not account/group-scoped, after an initial false start with a mistakenly-pasted account-level token, flagged for revocation, never used) and both Railway tokens (one per environment — PO provided one for each rather than prod-only; verified via GraphQL auth — distinct environmentId per token confirms real per-environment scoping). scripts/agent-diagnostics/turso-query.mjs and railway-query.sh (read-only query runners) + runbook. Railway's official CLI does not work in this sandbox (no Linux aarch64 build) — railway-query.sh uses direct GraphQL calls (Project-Access-Token header) as the documented fallback. ALSO FOUND AND FIXED (ADL-34, same PR): init-firewall.sh fail-open bug — one dead static domain (statsig.anthropic.com, NXDOMAIN) aborted the whole script before the default-DROP lockdown was ever applied, leaving the container's outbound network fully unrestricted every container start. Fixed by moving lockdown before domain resolution. FIRST REAL USE (same session) surfaced the actual root cause of the original stuck-deploy problem: the Railway project's plan is `trial`, and Railway was actively deprioritizing Trial/Hobby deploys platform-wide during a demand spike (2026-07-21, confirmed via Railway status/community reports) — not a code/config issue. Flagged to Ryan: confirm the Hobby-plan upgrade from ADL-32 actually completed; Pro tier is the only tier that fully bypasses the deploy queue. FOLLOW-UP (2026-07-21, ADL-34 §5): the container rebuild happened and surfaced a second bug in the same fix — GitHub itself failed the final verification (`unable to reach https://api.github.com`). Root cause: lockdown-before-resolution now blocks step 6's own `curl https://api.github.com/meta` bootstrap fetch (chicken-and-egg — GitHub's IPs aren't allowlisted yet because that fetch is what's supposed to allowlist them). Fixed by DNS-bootstrapping api.github.com's IP via `dig` (same pattern as the Turso/Railway entries) before the curl call. Not yet live-verified — needs another container rebuild. REMAINING: this second fix's own end-to-end verification via container rebuild.

2. Missing `db:migrate` before server start — ADL-32 §5 specified it, PR #175/#176 never wired it in, so the Turso prod DB was connected to but never schema-migrated. Fixed PR #185.

Frontend/Clerk env vars were never set on Railway at all initially; once added, Helmet's CSP (`scriptSrc: ["'self'"]`) blocked Clerk's browser SDK entirely (never exercised before since the frontend previously only ran via Vite's dev server, not this Express app). Fix: seed GB/'United Kingdom' with region_tier_enabled=1, region_tier_label likely 'Constituent Country', and add Scotland/England/Wales/Northern Ireland as regions. CONFIRMED both PRs fully green 2026-07-20: backend PR #166 ('remove-place cascade fix + confirm existing DELETE route' — DELETE route already existed, agent fixed cascade behavior instead of adding a new route) and frontend PR #170 ('add remove-place affordance to trip detail'), both Closes #156, all CI checks pass on each. Both PRs MERGED to main 2026-07-20 (PR #166 backend, PR #170 frontend, each squash), main CI confirmed green after both. items.title: Duplicate city entries in place autocomplete (Glasgow appeared twice)
items.notes: Found 2026-07-20 UAT. `cities` table has no uniqueness constraint on (name, country_code) — the geocoding/lookup path is creating a new row instead of finding the existing one. Fix: find-or-create by (name, country_code) case-insensitive, plus a unique index to prevent recurrence; needs a data cleanup pass for existing duplicates. GitHub issue #157. DISPATCHED 2026-07-20: database (branch fix/bug33-city-dedup-schema) + backend (branch fix/bug33-city-dedup-logic), parallel. Backend PR opened 2026-07-20: #167, Closes #157. POST /api/cities now finds-or-creates by (name, country_code) case-insensitive before inserting. 3 new tests + full suite green, CI mostly green (E2E pending as of this note). Independent of the parallel DB-brief unique index. Schema half PR opened 2026-07-20: #169, Closes #157, BRD GE-11, all 9 CI checks green. Adds UNIQUE(name COLLATE NOCASE, country_code) on cities (uniq_cities_name_country_ci) plus a data-cleanup migration merging existing duplicates (canonical = lowest id, geocode fields coalesced from best-resolved dup, trip_places/items/trip_place_activities_map re-pointed, collision with uniq_trip_places_trip_city handled by keeping the earlier trip_place row). Architect consulted before implementation per the schema-change-review rule (COLLATE NOCASE mechanism + trip_places collision-handling ruling). Verified against a throwaway copy of real dev.db duplicate data before writing the real migration. IMPORTANT for the parallel backend brief (fix/bug33-city-dedup-logic): its find-or-create lookup must match COLLATE NOCASE or it'll miss the canonical post-merge row and throw on insert. Schema half MERGED to main 2026-07-20 (PR #169, squash, renumbered to migrations 0009/0010 to resolve the BUG-30 idx collision), main CI confirmed green. Logic half (PR #167) hit a merge conflict, owning agent resolving as of this note. Logic half MERGED to main 2026-07-20 (PR #167, squash), main CI confirmed green post-merge. All 9 UAT-triage briefs from this session now fully merged.

items.notes: ADL-35 (2026-07-21, merged PR #193).
